note: Generated by generate.py. Signed with the vector key in jwks.json, for testing only. Outcomes: accept | reject (the Passport itself fails) | deny (revoked, or unable to tell) | refetch (fetch the current Passport and start again).

bindings in a different order with a duplicated entry; the presenter matches the last one (01 §3: no assumed order or distinctness).
status carries a second, unrecognized mechanism beside revocation_check: ignored.
Two entries in signatures, the second a copy of the first: v1 requires exactly one (01 §4).

Protected header typ is JOSE, as earlier drafts signed: still accepted (01 §4).
Protected header carries no typ: accepted (01 §4).
typ is the full media type in mixed case, Application/AI-Passport+JWS: compared case-insensitively (01 §4, RFC 7515 §4.1.9).

vectors.description: accountable lists an owner and no manager (01 §8.5).
The only manager entry carries neither principal nor name, so it reads as absent and there is no manager (01 §8.5).
The manager and org_unit are named by name alone, as a Passport served only to authenticated callers may be (01 §8.3, §10). The verifier authenticated the presenter and retrieved it; accepted.
parent is {}: a parent that cannot be resolved, treated as revoked (01 §3.4).
parent is null: no parent (01 §3.4).
parent.issuer differs from issuer: treated as revoked (01 §3.4).
A deployment's Passport naming its parent, with a member parent does not define: ignored, accepted (01 §3, §3.4).
status.revocation_check.uri is on another origin than issuer, and no responder is configured for it: treated as revoked, never called (01 §9.1).
status.revocation_check.uri is http on the issuer's host: not https, treated as revoked (01 §9.1).
As P46, but the verifier has configured that responder for this issuer (01 §9.1).
issuer is another configured issuer, whose key set does not hold k1; k1 is in the first issuer's key set. A kid in another issuer's JWKS never verifies (01 §9.1).
issuer is one the verifier is not configured with; the Passport names k1 (01 §9.1).
issuer differs from the configured issuer by a trailing slash: compared exactly, so no trust anchor (01 §9.1).
The presenter claims a pair listed in bindings but was not authenticated; the Passport was retrieved by that pair. Retrieval does not replace authentication (01 §3.3).
This Passport is the one refetch after a revision floor, and the floor is still above its revision: deny (01 §10, 02 §5.6).
This Passport is the one refetch after a revision floor; the presenter is not in bindings. One refetch per verification, whatever the trigger (01 §10).
issuance_class absent: optional, read as unknown, so a check that reads it does not pass (01 §3). Accepted. The kit has no policy step, so the unknown value is not exercised.
Protected header typ is jose, in lower case: compared case-insensitively (01 §4).
The decoded protected header repeats typ, JWT before ai-passport+jws. A last-wins parser accepts it; the header must be I-JSON (01 §4).

purpose.autonomy_level carries a value this version does not define. The Passport is accepted; the value compares as fully_automated, the most restrictive (01 §8.5, §8.7). The kit has no policy step, so the ordering is not exercised.
A binding in the earlier shape, its authority a bare string: not an object, so the entry is malformed (01 §3.3).
A binding whose authority carries neither id nor name (01 §3.3).
A binding whose authority.id is not an absolute URI, login.example.net/tenant-42 (01 §3.3).

The only binding for the presenter's identifier has authority.name alone, spelled like the authority the verifier authenticated. Retrieval by that URI compares it with authority.id only (01 §10), so this Passport came another way, as the one refetch; a binding without authority.id never attributes (01 §3.3).
The presenter matches a binding by authority.id; its name is another system's URL. Matching is on id and identifier only (01 §3.3).
A binding's authority carries a member this version does not define: ignored (01 §3); the presenter matches it.
type carries a value this version does not define, on the binding the presenter matches. It is informative and never matched (01 §3.3).
A cloud resource name, an AWS ARN, listed with authority.name alone, beside the binding the presenter matches. It serves lookup only and does not make the Passport malformed (01 §3.3).
issuance_class is null: read as absent, so unknown, not rejected (01 §3).
Protected header typ is application/jose, the full form of JOSE (01 §4, RFC 7515 §4.1.9).
The presenter matches a binding, but the configuration accepts from this issuer only its own instance URL as an authority, not the IdP (01 §9.1).
Two trusted issuers are both configured to bind the IdP, and the configuration does not rank them: deny (01 §9.1).
As P70, with this issuer ranked first: accepted (01 §9.1).
As P70, with the other issuer ranked first and not yet asked: deny (01 §9.1).
As P72, after the higher-ranked issuer's responder, asked by the pair, answered unresolved_identity: accepted (01 §9.1).
The presenter's identifier was resolved by a mapping the verifier is configured to trust, from the credential it authenticated: accepted (01 §3.3).
The presenter's identifier was taken from a value the presenter chose, such as a session name or a header: deny (01 §3.3).
As P73, but the higher-ranked issuer answered binding_revoked: it may hold the pair, so deny (01 §9.1).
As P73, but the higher-ranked issuer's responder timed out: deny (01 §9.1).
As P73, but the higher-ranked issuer answered 404 at retrieval: a lapse, a withdrawal or an ambiguity, not 'not mine', so deny (01 §9.1, §10).
Three issuers accept the IdP, this one ranked third; only the first answered unresolved_identity: deny (01 §9.1).
A shared authority, accepted from this issuer for tenant-42 only; the presenter authenticated in tenant-7: deny (01 §9.1).
As P80, the presenter authenticated in tenant-42: accepted (01 §9.1).
